summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.
summary.overview: Management reported operating revenue of Rs.167 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs.47 crore (+3%, margin 28.12%) for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs.172 crore (+10%) and EBITDA of Rs.52 crore (+8%). Occupancy held at 92%, but ADR growth was only about 2% amid West Asia disruption, weak international air traffic and flat domestic air traffic. PAT declined about 14% to close to Rs.12 crore, reflecting about Rs.2.5 crore higher finance charges from Zillion acquisition financing and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision on the move to the new tax regime. Management guided to a stronger ADR trend from Q2 onward, with the BRICS Summit, weddings and exhibitions cited as drivers.

segments.name: Food and Beverage
segments.commentary: F&B contributed about 43% of total revenue in Q1; Flurys stood at 111 outlets (cafes, kiosks, tea rooms) after adding one at Inorbit Mall Vizag, with first standalone North India cafe opened in Gurugram in August.

segments.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
segments.commentary: Portfolio stated as 42 hotels with 2,677 keys (one slide reference in call says 2,667). Ran Baas Patiala ARR about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace Chettinad about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata mixed-use project
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; expected cash inflow Rs.70-80 crore this year, of which Rs.21 crore received.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth guided to high single digits for the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show Bengaluru and Bharat Mobility Expo.
Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 from 2,677 keys.
Flurys target of 29 additional outlets in FY27, taking count to about 140; target of 400 outlets by 2030.
Long-term ambition of more than 6,000 keys by FY2030; management also cited 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Other income guided at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter; further cash inflow of about Rs.50 crore expected from EM Bypass by year-end.
Effective tax rate guided to fall to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under the new regime (from about 40% in Q1).
capex_capacity: EM Bypass Kolkata: 218 hotel rooms plus 69 service apartments, completion targeted early 2030; second Kolkata hotel referenced for opening in 2030.
The Park Juhu (78 rooms, converted from service apartments): design complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for Zillion acquisition.
Vizag 100-room hotel: on site, launch expected in August 2026, completion early 2030.
Malabar House, Fort Kochi (17 keys, about half an acre): acquisition in progress, completion expected October-November 2026; acquisition cost about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI raised from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan of 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential.

Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years: about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus Zillion acquisition about Rs.210 crore, Juhu renovation about Rs.80 crore and Kochi about Rs.64 crore (total about Rs.350 crore additional, cited with EM Bypass funding offset). Operating capex Rs.40 crore per year plus Flurys Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore per year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex expected within FY27.
Completed SAP S/4HANA implementation for Finance during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; RevPAR leadership in upper upscale maintained.

Management said All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter, versus about 2% for the company as stated in analyst question; domestic passenger traffic flat and international inbound air traffic down about 10%.
City-level domestic passenger declines cited: Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%.
Juhu ARR about Rs.18,000-20,000; management expects Bombay ARR growth of 10-15%.
Management expects ADR to improve from Q2 onward; said Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.
Pricing on EM Bypass service apartments: average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; Juhu acquisition at about Rs.40,000 per sq ft versus market levels cited near Rs.1 lakh per sq ft.
